raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Attention sinks were previously loaded through model-specific `load_weights` logic. These direct writes bypassed the standard `weight_loader` pipeline, leaving stale sink values after layerwise reload during RL weight updates.

This change registers checkpoint-backed attention sinks with a common `load_attention_sink` weight loader in `model_loader/weight_utils.py`, and adds `make_attention_sink()`, which creates the sink parameter with `-inf` padding and registers that loader in one place. DeepSeek V4/V4.1, HY-V4, MiMo-V2, GPT-OSS, Laguna, and Qwen3-DFlash build their sinks through the factory and load them through their normal parameter loading paths. MiMo-V2 MTP and its Omni MTP subclass no longer pre-slice sinks before the common loader, which previously caused double TP sharding after the attention parameter was migrated. GPT-OSS sinks use the parameter loader across MXFP4, Quark, and other quantization paths; quantization-specific handling stays confined to quantized weights.

The loader validates one-dimensional shapes, rejects an empty sink checkpoint instead of silently disabling the sink, reports the offending head counts when the checkpoint is not divisible by the TP size or does not fit the runtime parameter, takes the TP-local head slice, and restores any runtime padding to `-inf` on every load — the old per-model copies never rewrote the padded heads. Unpadded sinks (GPT-OSS, MiMo-V2, Laguna, Qwen3-DFlash) are loaded in place without rebuilding the tensor. Its documentation records the even-head-partition assumption; uneven TP partitions require explicit head-range handling in a future extension.

## Consolidation

This PR replaces the split attention-sink series: #57798, #57801, #57803, #57804, #57805, and #57806. It rebuilds the implementation on current upstream `main` around parameter-level weight loading instead of squashing the model-specific fixes. The sibling PRs are superseded, so this is the single review target for the fix.

## Tests

- `test_attention_sink_uses_common_factory` checks that every sink model creates its parameter through `make_attention_sink`; a hand-built parameter would bypass the `-inf` padding and the registered loader. It replaces the earlier audit that imported and executed production statements.
- `test_attention_sink_model_loading_shards_once` calls the real model loading entry points (MiMo-V2 MTP, Omni MTP, Laguna, Qwen3-DFlash) and checks the parameter loader receives the unsliced global checkpoint exactly once.
- `test_gpt_oss_attention_sink_uses_parameter_loader` is renamed so that `-k attention_sink` selects it (it was previously missed by that filter), and covers MXFP4, Quark and the unquantized path. `test_gpt_oss_attention_sink_skips_missing_parameter` covers the pipeline-parallel skip path, the only guard the removal of the per-model sink branches leaves implicit.
- `test_attention_sink_layerwise_reload` covers both TP ranks, padded and exact runtime shapes, cold loading, two live updates, restored padding, and preservation of the sink storage referenced by kernels.
- Loader unit tests in `tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py`: exact/padded shapes across every rank at TP=1/2/4, invalid dimensionality, empty checkpoint, uneven head counts, oversized local shards, padding restore, dtype cast, CPU checkpoint to CUDA parameter, and the factory contract.

## Validation on H20

Environment: H20 Slurm cluster, node `vllm-h20-02`, 2 x NVIDIA H20-3e, driver 580.105.08; Python 3.12.14 / torch 2.13.0+cu130. Compiled extensions come from the per-commit precompiled cu130 wheel built for this PR's base commit (`vllm-0.31.1rc1.dev295+gd4e92ccc3`) with the branch's Python files overlaid, so Python and extensions are from the same commit without a rebuild.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k sink -q` | **41 passed** (GPU node) |
| full `test_weight_utils.py` + `test_reload.py`, this branch | 18 failed, **110 passed**, 14 skipped, 2 xfailed, 7 errors |
| full same two files at upstream `main` (control) | 18 failed, 70 passed, 13 skipped, 2 xfailed, 7 errors |
| failure-name diff, main -> branch | **identical set** (25 names); every additional pass is a sink test |
| `run-precommit.sh` (every hook the diff touches) | exit 0, no file rewritten |
| DCO over the branch range | all commits signed off, `DCO pass` |

The failures are model-download / multi-GPU cases that fail identically before and after the change, so they carry no signal about this PR.

Additional out-of-tree verification (harness deliberately kept outside the PR, results in the review comments): each sink model's real attention module was built from tiny dimensions with dummy weights on H20, for TP=1 and TP=2, and driven through the real layerwise reload lifecycle, asserting the per-rank slice, the `-inf` padding and the preserved kernel storage; the pre-PR loading shape was reproduced as a control and never received the reloaded sinks.

## Not verified

- No full-model accuracy evaluation: no DeepSeek V4/V4.1, HY-V4, MiMo-V2, Laguna or Qwen3-DFlash checkpoints are available here, and `openai/gpt-oss-20b` (13 GB) could not be downloaded at usable speed. The out-of-tree runs use real model code with dummy weights, not real checkpoints, and the DeepSeek V4.1 case there builds a plain layer rather than a compressed one (its indexer cache needs DeepGEMM sparse MQA).
- Pipeline parallelism is covered through the skip-path test only; TP>2 and multi-node were not exercised.
- FlashInfer and b12x keep a converted fp32 copy of a non-fp32 sink (`process_weights_after_loading` refreshes it), which the current reload flow calls for attention layers. That coupling is unchanged by this PR and is not covered by a test.

AI assistance was used.

﻿## Verification on H20 (attention-sink series)

Verification of this PR used an integrated tree containing all six fix PRs, so the shared helper and every call site were exercised together.

**Verified commit:** `64c77ee60341e1aa51af3405a20934dfcd2ec8f2` (this PR's head, which is the shared helper plus the CUDA reload test)
**Integration commit:** `c623df9e4bfe1133a3205b94e2d771ba43876ec7` (`attn-sink-integration` = #57797 + #57798 + #57801 + #57803 + #57804 + #57805 + #57806)

### Environment

- Cluster: H20 Slurm, node `vllm-h20-01`, 1x NVIDIA H20-3e, `--partition=h20 --gres=gpu:h20:1`
- Python: `$HOME/vllm-shared/prebuilt-venv/bin/python` (torch 2.13.0+cu130, compiled vllm from the shared prebuilt baseline)
- The change is pure Python, so the verified revision was overlaid onto the prebuilt package with `make-overlay.sh`; no recompilation was needed.
- CPU run: H20 head node, same overlay, CPU torch only.

### Results

| Suite | Where | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_attention_sink_load_audit.py` | head node (CPU) | 39 passed |
| `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_attn_sink_reload.py` | head node (CPU) | 18 passed, 2 skipped (CUDA-only cases) |
| `test_attn_sink_reload.py` | H20 GPU | **20 passed** (the two CUDA cases run and pass) |
| GPU end-to-end sink reload script | H20 GPU | **8/8 checks passed** |

GPU end-to-end output (real layerwise reload on device storage):

```text
PASS  cold load is on device
PASS  cold load writes local heads
PASS  cold load keeps -inf padding
PASS  live update reaches kernel tensor
PASS  live update re-establishes -inf padding
PASS  kernel tensor storage is stable

ALL GPU SINK CHECKS PASSED
```

Command: `PYTHONPATH=<overlay> python -m pytest -q --import-mode=importlib <overlay>/tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_attn_sink_reload.py`

### Pre-commit

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` on this branch, run twice to prove idempotence:

```text
pass1 rc=0 dirty=0
pass2 rc=0 dirty=0
```

`ruff check`, `ruff format`, `check-spdx-header`, `check-test-tethering`, `mypy` (3.10-3.13) and the remaining hooks all pass; no hook rewrote a file. `run-precommit.sh` skips the `pip-compile` hooks because the sandbox cannot reach PyPI to build `encodec`/`rouge-score`/`jsmin`; no requirements file is touched by this PR.

### Not verified

- No full-model checkpoint was loaded (no DeepSeek V4/V4.1/HY-V4/MiMo/GPT-OSS weights are available here), so this is a loader/contract-level verification plus a real GPU reload, not a full-model accuracy run.
- Run on one H20 node; TP>1 was exercised in-process by driving distinct rank head ranges, not as a multi-process TP run.

### What changed in this revision

- The helper moved out of `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/sink.py` into `vllm/model_executor/model_loader/attention_sink.py`, next to `default_weight_loader`. It is part of the loading interface that HY-V4 loads through, so it does not belong under one model package.
- The reconstructed runtime tensor is built with `torch.empty(param.shape, dtype=param.dtype, device=local_weight.device)` instead of `torch.full(..., -inf, dtype=...)` plus an implicit dtype cast, so a checkpoint/parameter dtype mismatch is resolved before the load rather than relied on implicitly. Dtype coverage added.
- A head range wider than the padded parameter now raises `ValueError` instead of silently truncating; this is the one way the old shape could load the wrong heads. Coverage added.
- Added a CUDA-parametrized case to the reload suite (`torch.cuda.is_available()` skip guard) so CI exercises the device boundary, not just CPU. It passes on H20 (see above).

## Lightweight integration audit and validation

Updated commit: `01b4adb1236fcdb38bc8c171d302600089a29750`.

Added two parameterized checks to the existing `test_reload.py` suite:

- `test_attention_sink_weight_loader_registration`: covers DeepSeek V4, DeepSeek V4.1, HY-V4, MiMo-V2, and GPT-OSS. It checks the common-loader import and executes only the production sink declaration and registration statements, then inspects the resulting parameter's loader. Full attention constructors, checkpoints, and inference are not involved.
- `test_gpt_oss_sink_uses_parameter_loader`: calls the real `GptOssModel.load_weights()` on a minimal parameter container for `mxfp4`, `quark`, and the other/unquantized path. A spy installed as the parameter's current loader must receive the checkpoint exactly once, and the sink must contain the loaded values. Restoring a direct sink copy would fail this check.

### Results

Local isolated CPU execution: **21 passed**.

| Coverage | Passed |
| --- | ---: |
| Common layerwise reload regression | 4 |
| Loader shape cases (all ranks at TP=1/2/4) | 4 |
| Invalid-input cases | 5 |
| Migrated model registrations | 5 |
| GPT-OSS quantization dispatch paths | 3 |

Command: `uv run --no-project <local-venv-python> -m pytest --confcutdir=.validation .validation/test_sink_isolated.py -q`.

The temporary local harness executes the exact repository test functions with real PyTorch. It loads the unchanged reload modules, production sink initialization statements, and actual GPT-OSS loading methods and relevant helpers extracted from source, while bypassing unrelated vLLM startup imports. Logging/configuration, attention classification, and the quantization base class use stand-ins. This result is isolated verification, not a successful standard-suite or full-model run; the harness is not added to the PR.

Sensitivity check: **all 8 intentional regressions were detected** — removing the sink registration from each of the five models, and bypassing the parameter loader with direct copies in each of the three GPT-OSS loading paths. These mutations were in-memory only and were not committed.

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `git diff --check`, SPDX, forbidden-import, and test-tethering checks passed for the changed test file. The new tests remain in an existing CI-selected suite.

Standard command attempted:

```text
pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py -k attention_sink -q
```

It remains blocked during `tests/conftest.py` import by `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'uvloop'` in the local Windows environment. The previously reported complete pre-commit limitation also remains. No GPU execution, full-model accuracy evaluation, multi-process TP run, or remote H20 validation was performed for this update.

## Sink loading-path follow-up

Updated commit: `6e171163ab008e15e7eca49f884633a66f26e3a8` (signed off; upstream `main` merged before committing).

The broader audit found a missed MiMo-V2 MTP path: it pre-sliced `attention_sink_bias` and then called the newly registered common loader, causing double TP sharding. At TP=2 with checkpoint `[0,...,7]`, the old path produced `[0,1,-inf,-inf]` and `[6,7,-inf,-inf]` instead of `[0,1,2,3]` and `[4,5,6,7]`. Removing this pre-slicing also fixes the inherited `MiMoV2OmniMTP` path.

Laguna and Qwen3-DFlash now register `load_attention_sink` on their sink parameters and pass the original checkpoint to normal loading. Their model-level sink preprocessing helpers were removed. The replicated visual sink in MiMo-V2 Omni and the multidimensional OpenPangu sink K/V parameters retain their existing loading contracts.

Test changes:

- Registration audit extended from five to seven attention implementations, adding Laguna and Qwen3-DFlash.
- One shared `test_attention_sink_model_loading_shards_once` covers MiMo-V2 MTP, Omni MTP, Laguna, and Qwen3-DFlash on both TP ranks. It calls the actual model loading entry points on minimal parameter containers, checks that the parameter loader receives the unsliced global checkpoint, and verifies cold-load values, layerwise reload values, and original sink storage.

Validation:

- Local isolated CPU execution: **31 passed** — 7 registration, 8 model loading-path, 3 GPT-OSS quant-path, 4 common reload, 4 shape, and 5 invalid-input cases.
- Restoring the old pre-slicing implementations in memory causes all **8** new loading-path cases to fail, confirming sensitivity to the reported regression.
- Ruff lint/format, diff whitespace, SPDX, forbidden-import, and CI test-tethering checks passed.
- Standard pytest was attempted again and remains blocked during `tests/conftest.py` import because the local Windows environment lacks `uvloop`. Complete pre-commit remains subject to the previously documented Windows hook limitation.

The temporary isolated harness executes the exact test functions with real PyTorch, the real reload modules and decorator, and production `AutoWeightsLoader`, `WeightsMapper`, model loading methods, and helpers extracted from source. Unrelated startup/platform dependencies and embedding/missing-layer types use stand-ins. The harness is not part of the PR, and these results do not constitute a standard-suite or full-model run. No remote H20, GPU execution, full-model evaluation, or multi-process TP run was performed.

## Independent verification on H20 (PR head `6e171163ab`)

Filling the gap left in my previous comment: this commit had only isolated-harness results, so the repository suites, a real multi-process TP run, and a real model run were executed on the cluster.

**Verified commit:** `6e171163ab008e15e7eca49f884633a66f26e3a8` (PR head, unchanged — nothing was pushed).
**Base used for diffs and the control run:** `d4e92ccc37e67048a957aa8e08dc5a2bc665f422`.

### Environment

- H20 Slurm cluster, node `vllm-h20-02`, 2 x NVIDIA H20-3e (143 GB), driver 580.105.08; head node for the CPU runs.
- Python 3.12.14, torch 2.13.0+cu130 (shared `prebuilt-venv`).
- Compiled extensions: the per-commit precompiled cu130 wheel built for **this PR's own base commit** (`vllm-0.31.1rc1.dev295+gd4e92ccc3`), with the PR head's 26 changed `vllm/` files symlinked over it, so Python and extensions come from the same commit — no rebuild. Earlier runs over the shared Sep-24 prebuilt package gave the same test results.

### Results

| Check | Where | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k sink -q` | head node (CPU), GPU node, wheel env | **31 passed** (three independent runs) |
| `... -k attention_sink -q` (the filter in the PR description) | — | selects **28** of 31; see note 1 |
| full `test_weight_utils.py` + `test_reload.py` (PR head) | H20, 1 GPU | 14 failed, **104 passed**, 22 skipped, 1 xfailed |

### Real TP=2 run (no monkeypatched rank)

`torchrun --nproc_per_node=2` + `init_distributed_environment` / `initialize_model_parallel`; each rank reads `get_tensor_model_parallel_rank()` from a real process group.

```text
[rank0] PASS  tp identity is the real rank  (tp_rank=0 tp_size=2 rank=0 world=2)
[rank1] PASS  cold load takes the rank's own head slice  (got [4.0,5.0,6.0,7.0] expected [4.0,5.0,6.0,7.0])
[rank0] PASS  cold load takes the rank's own head slice  (got [0.0,1.0,2.0,3.0] expected [0.0,1.0,2.0,3.0])
[rank0] PASS  cold load fills padding with -inf / keeps the sink on device (cuda:0)
[rank0] PASS  reload updates the kernel tensor in place  (got [100,101,102,103] expected ...)
[rank1] PASS  reload updates the kernel tensor in place  (got [104,105,106,107] expected ...)
[rank0] PASS  reload preserves the sink storage  (ptr=139881288306176 old=139881288306176)
[rank0] PASS  reload re-establishes -inf padding
[rank0] PASS  gathered rank slices reconstruct the global checkpoint
TP=2 sink checks: ALL PASSED
```

The same script contains a control that reproduces the pre-PR loading shape (indexed `params[name][:n].copy_(...)`, no `weight_loader`). After a layerwise reload it never receives the new checkpoint values — it keeps the old value or, for a non-deferred layer, uninitialized materialized memory:

```text
[rank0] PASS  control: legacy direct copy never applies the reloaded sinks
        (after [0.0,0.0,0.0,0.0] cold [0.0,1.0,2.0,3.0] new [100,101,102,103])
[rank1] PASS  control: legacy direct copy never applies the reloaded sinks
        (after [1.6e-24,0.0,5.4e-41,0.0] cold [4.0,5.0,6.0,7.0] new [104,105,106,107])
```

The mechanism is `copy_` into a meta tensor being a silent no-op (`torch.empty(4, device="meta").copy_(x)` raises nothing), so the direct write disappears during reload while the wrapped loaders are replayed. This confirms the bug premise of the PR at the mechanism level.

### Real model end-to-end (tiny gpt-oss, real kernels)

`openai/gpt-oss-20b` (13 GB) could not be fetched at usable speed (HF without a token, ~0.5 MB/s), so the end-to-end run uses a 2-layer `GptOssForCausalLM` with the real architecture, tokenizer and attention backend, dummy-initialized weights, and the real `GptOssModel.load_weights` / layerwise reload paths:

```text
===== tiny gpt-oss end-to-end, TP=2 =====
  PASS  rank0: load_weights returns exactly the sink parameters  (2 params)
  PASS  rank0: sink holds its own global head slice
  PASS  rank0: attention impl reads the storage the loader writes  (per-layer [True, True])
  PASS  rank0: reload moves the sinks to meta
  PASS  rank0: reload updates the sink in place  (values [25,26,27,28] expected [25,26,27,28])
  PASS  rank1: reload updates the sink in place  (values [29,30,31,32] expected [29,30,31,32])
  PASS  rank0/rank1: reload preserves the sink storage (ptr unchanged)
  PASS  engine still generates tokens after the sink reload
ALL E2E SINK CHECKS PASSED
```

The two ranks holding different slices (`25..28` vs `29..32`) after a full reload is the per-rank sharding check on a real model; `attn.impl.sinks` sharing `data_ptr` with `attn.sinks` confirms the tensor the kernel reads is the one the loader writes.

### Review notes

1. **The command in the PR description misses 3 of the 31 new cases.** `-k attention_sink` does not match `test_gpt_oss_sink_uses_parameter_loader[mxfp4|quark|None]`; `--collect-only` reports 28 vs 31. `-k sink` selects all 31. Worth fixing in the PR body (and it is why my earlier harness number was 31 while the documented command reports 28).
2. `test_attention_sink_weight_loader_registration` asserts the *source text* (AST parse, then `exec` of the declaration plus the immediately following statement). It is sensitive to statement order, import form and checkout layout rather than behaviour, and `exec`ing production source in a test is unusual here; a refactor that keeps the registration but moves it (or uses `set_weight_attrs`) would fail it. The other new tests already assert the behaviour, so this one could be dropped or reduced to the models the loading-path test does not cover.
3. Loading-path coverage is partial: `test_attention_sink_model_loading_shards_once` covers MiMo-V2 MTP/Omni MTP, Laguna and Qwen3-DFlash, while the DeepSeek V4/V4.1 call sites (target, MTP, dspark, cpu/xpu/amd) and HY-V4 (target + MTP) that this PR also migrated have no equivalent check. I verified by inspection that all of them fall through to a generic `getattr(param, "weight_loader", default_weight_loader)` branch that keeps the `is_pp_missing_parameter` guard, so the removals are structurally safe, but the regression would not be caught if it came back in one of those files.
4. Equivalence looks correct: the helper reproduces the removed slicing exactly for the even-partition case (`loaded_weight.numel() // tp_size` at `tp_rank`), is stricter than the old code (rejects non-1-D, empty, non-divisible and oversized-local), and additionally rewrites the `-inf` padding after reload, which the old code never did. No cold-load behaviour change found.
5. Sink holders deliberately left alone check out: `granite`/`granitemoe` already register `sharded_weight_loader(0)`, and `mimo_v2_omni`'s replicated `sinks` is loaded through `AutoWeightsLoader` with the default loader, so both already participate in reload.

### Not verified

- No full-model accuracy/eval for the models this PR touches — no DeepSeek V4/V4.1, HY-V4, MiMo-V2, Laguna or Qwen3-DFlash checkpoints are available here, and gpt-oss-20b could not be downloaded.
- The end-to-end model run proves the real model class, loader dispatch, TP sharding and reload lifecycle, but with dummy weights, so it is not an accuracy check.
- Pipeline parallelism, TP>2 and multi-node were not exercised.
- Harness scripts and logs: `~/vllm-tasks/pr57797/{gpu,logs}` on the H20 head node (`pr57797-sink4-4945.log`, `pr57797-e2e-4948.log`, `pr57797-suite-4946.log`). Environment facts discovered on the way (the Sep-24 shared prebuilt cannot run any MoE model: `_moe_C::moe_align_block_size` compiled for 7 args vs 8 in its own Python) are recorded in `~/vllm-shared/README.md`.

AI assistance was used for this verification.

## Revision: shared sink factory + real tiny-model coverage (verified on H20)

Pushed `421201007d` (fast-forward on top of the previous head). Addressing the review suggestions from my earlier verification comment, leaving point 5 (the FlashInfer/b12x fp32-copy coupling) untouched as agreed.

**Code**

- `make_attention_sink(num_heads, dtype=None)` now creates the sink parameter with `-inf` in its padded heads and registers `load_attention_sink` on it, and all seven sites use it (DeepSeek V4/V4.1, HY-V4, GPT-OSS, MiMo-V2, Laguna, Qwen3-DFlash). - `load_attention_sink` reports the offending head counts, rejects an empty checkpoint as its own error (an empty sink would otherwise silently disable the sink), loads unpadded sinks in place without the extra `cat`, and restores `-inf` padding with an explicit fill. Docstring now carries `Raises:` plus the padding and even-partition contracts.
- The `-k attention_sink` filter missed three cases; `test_gpt_oss_sink_uses_parameter_loader` is renamed so the documented command selects it.

- New pipeline-parallel skip test, padding-restore / dtype-cast / CPU-to-CUDA / factory unit tests in `tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py`.

detail.body:
Attention sinks were previously loaded through model-specific `load_weights` logic. These direct writes bypassed the standard `weight_loader` pipeline, leaving stale sink values after layerwise reload during RL weight updates.

This change registers checkpoint-backed attention sinks with a common `load_attention_sink` weight loader in `model_loader/weight_utils.py`, and adds `make_attention_sink()`, which creates the sink parameter with `-inf` padding and registers that loader in one place. DeepSeek V4/V4.1, HY-V4, MiMo-V2, GPT-OSS, Laguna, and Qwen3-DFlash build their sinks through the factory and load them through their normal parameter loading paths. MiMo-V2 MTP and its Omni MTP subclass no longer pre-slice sinks before the common loader, which previously caused double TP sharding after the attention parameter was migrated. GPT-OSS sinks use the parameter loader across MXFP4, Quark, and other quantization paths; quantization-specific handling stays confined to quantized weights.

The loader validates one-dimensional shapes, rejects an empty sink checkpoint instead of silently disabling the sink, reports the offending head counts when the checkpoint is not divisible by the TP size or does not fit the runtime parameter, takes the TP-local head slice, and restores any runtime padding to `-inf` on every load — the old per-model copies never rewrote the padded heads. Unpadded sinks (GPT-OSS, MiMo-V2, Laguna, Qwen3-DFlash) are loaded in place without rebuilding the tensor. Its documentation records the even-head-partition assumption; uneven TP partitions require explicit head-range handling in a future extension.

## Consolidation

This PR replaces the split attention-sink series: #57798, #57801, #57803, #57804, #57805, and #57806. It rebuilds the implementation on current upstream `main` around parameter-level weight loading instead of squashing the model-specific fixes. The sibling PRs are superseded, so this is the single review target for the fix.

## Tests

- `test_attention_sink_uses_common_factory` checks that every sink model creates its parameter through `make_attention_sink`; a hand-built parameter would bypass the `-inf` padding and the registered loader. It replaces the earlier audit that imported and executed production statements.
- `test_attention_sink_model_loading_shards_once` calls the real model loading entry points (MiMo-V2 MTP, Omni MTP, Laguna, Qwen3-DFlash) and checks the parameter loader receives the unsliced global checkpoint exactly once.
- `test_gpt_oss_attention_sink_uses_parameter_loader` is renamed so that `-k attention_sink` selects it (it was previously missed by that filter), and covers MXFP4, Quark and the unquantized path. `test_gpt_oss_attention_sink_skips_missing_parameter` covers the pipeline-parallel skip path, the only guard the removal of the per-model sink branches leaves implicit.
- `test_attention_sink_layerwise_reload` covers both TP ranks, padded and exact runtime shapes, cold loading, two live updates, restored padding, and preservation of the sink storage referenced by kernels.
- Loader unit tests in `tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py`: exact/padded shapes across every rank at TP=1/2/4, invalid dimensionality, empty checkpoint, uneven head counts, oversized local shards, padding restore, dtype cast, CPU checkpoint to CUDA parameter, and the factory contract.

## Validation on H20

Environment: H20 Slurm cluster, node `vllm-h20-02`, 2 x NVIDIA H20-3e, driver 580.105.08; Python 3.12.14 / torch 2.13.0+cu130. Compiled extensions come from the per-commit precompiled cu130 wheel built for this PR's base commit (`vllm-0.31.1rc1.dev295+gd4e92ccc3`) with the branch's Python files overlaid, so Python and extensions are from the same commit without a rebuild.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pytest tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k sink -q` | **41 passed** (GPU node) |
| full `test_weight_utils.py` + `test_reload.py`, this branch | 18 failed, **110 passed**, 14 skipped, 2 xfailed, 7 errors |
| full same two files at upstream `main` (control) | 18 failed, 70 passed, 13 skipped, 2 xfailed, 7 errors |
| failure-name diff, main -> branch | **identical set** (25 names); every additional pass is a sink test |
| `run-precommit.sh` (every hook the diff touches) | exit 0, no file rewritten |
| DCO over the branch range | all commits signed off, `DCO pass` |

The failures are model-download / multi-GPU cases that fail identically before and after the change, so they carry no signal about this PR.

Additional out-of-tree verification (harness deliberately kept outside the PR, results in the review comments): each sink model's real attention module was built from tiny dimensions with dummy weights on H20, for TP=1 and TP=2, and driven through the real layerwise reload lifecycle, asserting the per-rank slice, the `-inf` padding and the preserved kernel storage; the pre-PR loading shape was reproduced as a control and never received the reloaded sinks.

## Not verified

- No full-model accuracy evaluation: no DeepSeek V4/V4.1, HY-V4, MiMo-V2, Laguna or Qwen3-DFlash checkpoints are available here, and `openai/gpt-oss-20b` (13 GB) could not be downloaded at usable speed. The out-of-tree runs use real model code with dummy weights, not real checkpoints, and the DeepSeek V4.1 case there builds a plain layer rather than a compressed one (its indexer cache needs DeepGEMM sparse MQA).
- Pipeline parallelism is covered through the skip-path test only; TP>2 and multi-node were not exercised.
- FlashInfer and b12x keep a converted fp32 copy of a non-fp32 sink (`process_weights_after_loading` refreshes it), which the current reload flow calls for attention layers. That coupling is unchanged by this PR and is not covered by a test.

AI assistance was used.

+def load_attention_sink(param: torch.Tensor, loaded_weight: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+    """Load global sink heads into a TP-local parameter, padding with -inf.
+
+    Attention sinks are checkpoint-backed parameters and must participate in
+    the standard weight_loader pipeline. Register this on the parameter - see
+    ``make_attention_sink`` - so layerwise reload can replay sharding and shape
+    adaptation during RL weight updates. Model-specific load_weights copies
+    bypass that lifecycle.
+
+    The runtime sink must keep ``-inf`` in its padded heads; this loader
+    restores that invariant on every load. Checkpoint heads are assumed to be
+    evenly partitioned across tensor-parallel ranks, so models with uneven
+    partitions need explicit head ranges here.
+
+    Args:
+        param: One-dimensional runtime sink, optionally padded.
+        loaded_weight: One-dimensional checkpoint sink containing all heads.
+
+    Raises:
+        ValueError: If either tensor is not one-dimensional, if the checkpoint
+            sink is empty, if its head count is not divisible by the
+            tensor-parallel size, or if a rank's head range does not fit the
+            runtime parameter.
+
+    """
+    tp_size = get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size()
+    tp_rank = get_tensor_model_parallel_rank()
+    if param.ndim != 1 or loaded_weight.ndim != 1:
+        raise ValueError("Attention sinks must be one-dimensional")
+    heads = loaded_weight.numel()
+    if heads == 0:
+        # An empty sink is not a valid checkpoint: loading it would leave every
+        # runtime head at -inf, silently disabling the sink.
+        raise ValueError("Attention sink checkpoint is empty")
+    if heads % tp_size:

+            f"Attention sink heads ({heads}) must be divisible by tp_size ({tp_size})"
+        )
+    local_heads = heads // tp_size

+            f"parameter size ({param.numel()})"

+    default_weight_loader(param[:local_heads], local_weight)

﻿## Verification on H20 (attention-sink series)

Verification of this PR used an integrated tree containing all six fix PRs, so the shared helper and every call site were exercised together.

**Verified commit:** `64c77ee60341e1aa51af3405a20934dfcd2ec8f2` (this PR's head, which is the shared helper plus the CUDA reload test)
**Integration commit:** `c623df9e4bfe1133a3205b94e2d771ba43876ec7` (`attn-sink-integration` = #57797 + #57798 + #57801 + #57803 + #57804 + #57805 + #57806)

### Environment

- Cluster: H20 Slurm, node `vllm-h20-01`, 1x NVIDIA H20-3e, `--partition=h20 --gres=gpu:h20:1`
- Python: `$HOME/vllm-shared/prebuilt-venv/bin/python` (torch 2.13.0+cu130, compiled vllm from the shared prebuilt baseline)
- The change is pure Python, so the verified revision was overlaid onto the prebuilt package with `make-overlay.sh`; no recompilation was needed.
- CPU run: H20 head node, same overlay, CPU torch only.

### Results

| Suite | Where | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_attention_sink_load_audit.py` | head node (CPU) | 39 passed |
| `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_attn_sink_reload.py` | head node (CPU) | 18 passed, 2 skipped (CUDA-only cases) |
| `test_attn_sink_reload.py` | H20 GPU | **20 passed** (the two CUDA cases run and pass) |
| GPU end-to-end sink reload script | H20 GPU | **8/8 checks passed** |

GPU end-to-end output (real layerwise reload on device storage):

```text
PASS  cold load is on device
PASS  cold load writes local heads
PASS  cold load keeps -inf padding
PASS  live update reaches kernel tensor
PASS  live update re-establishes -inf padding
PASS  kernel tensor storage is stable
PASS  rank 1 live update loads its own heads
PASS  rank 1 keeps -inf padding
ALL GPU SINK CHECKS PASSED
```

Command: `PYTHONPATH=<overlay> python -m pytest -q --import-mode=importlib <overlay>/tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_attn_sink_reload.py`

### Pre-commit

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` on this branch, run twice to prove idempotence:

```text
pass1 rc=0 dirty=0
pass2 rc=0 dirty=0
```

`ruff check`, `ruff format`, `check-spdx-header`, `check-test-tethering`, `mypy` (3.10-3.13) and the remaining hooks all pass; no hook rewrote a file. `run-precommit.sh` skips the `pip-compile` hooks because the sandbox cannot reach PyPI to build `encodec`/`rouge-score`/`jsmin`; no requirements file is touched by this PR.

### Not verified

- No full-model checkpoint was loaded (no DeepSeek V4/V4.1/HY-V4/MiMo/GPT-OSS weights are available here), so this is a loader/contract-level verification plus a real GPU reload, not a full-model accuracy run.
- Run on one H20 node; TP>1 was exercised in-process by driving distinct rank head ranges, not as a multi-process TP run.

### What changed in this revision

- The helper moved out of `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/sink.py` into `vllm/model_executor/model_loader/attention_sink.py`, next to `default_weight_loader`. It is part of the loading interface that HY-V4 loads through, so it does not belong under one model package.
- The reconstructed runtime tensor is built with `torch.empty(param.shape, dtype=param.dtype, device=local_weight.device)` instead of `torch.full(..., -inf, dtype=...)` plus an implicit dtype cast, so a checkpoint/parameter dtype mismatch is resolved before the load rather than relied on implicitly. Dtype coverage added.
- A head range wider than the padded parameter now raises `ValueError` instead of silently truncating; this is the one way the old shape could load the wrong heads. Coverage added.
- Added a CUDA-parametrized case to the reload suite (`torch.cuda.is_available()` skip guard) so CI exercises the device boundary, not just CPU. It passes on H20 (see above).

## Lightweight integration audit and validation

Updated commit: `01b4adb1236fcdb38bc8c171d302600089a29750`.

Added two parameterized checks to the existing `test_reload.py` suite:

- `test_attention_sink_weight_loader_registration`: covers DeepSeek V4, DeepSeek V4.1, HY-V4, MiMo-V2, and GPT-OSS. It checks the common-loader import and executes only the production sink declaration and registration statements, then inspects the resulting parameter's loader. Full attention constructors, checkpoints, and inference are not involved.
- `test_gpt_oss_sink_uses_parameter_loader`: calls the real `GptOssModel.load_weights()` on a minimal parameter container for `mxfp4`, `quark`, and the other/unquantized path. A spy installed as the parameter's current loader must receive the checkpoint exactly once, and the sink must contain the loaded values. Restoring a direct sink copy would fail this check.

### Results

Local isolated CPU execution: **21 passed**.

| Coverage | Passed |
| --- | ---: |
| Common layerwise reload regression | 4 |
| Loader shape cases (all ranks at TP=1/2/4) | 4 |
| Invalid-input cases | 5 |
| Migrated model registrations | 5 |
| GPT-OSS quantization dispatch paths | 3 |

Command: `uv run --no-project <local-venv-python> -m pytest --confcutdir=.validation .validation/test_sink_isolated.py -q`.

The temporary local harness executes the exact repository test functions with real PyTorch. It loads the unchanged reload modules, production sink initialization statements, and actual GPT-OSS loading methods and relevant helpers extracted from source, while bypassing unrelated vLLM startup imports. Logging/configuration, attention classification, and the quantization base class use stand-ins. This result is isolated verification, not a successful standard-suite or full-model run; the harness is not added to the PR.

Sensitivity check: **all 8 intentional regressions were detected** — removing the sink registration from each of the five models, and bypassing the parameter loader with direct copies in each of the three GPT-OSS loading paths. These mutations were in-memory only and were not committed.

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `git diff --check`, SPDX, forbidden-import, and test-tethering checks passed for the changed test file. The new tests remain in an existing CI-selected suite.

Standard command attempted:


It remains blocked during `tests/conftest.py` import by `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'uvloop'` in the local Windows environment. The previously reported complete pre-commit limitation also remains. No GPU execution, full-model accuracy evaluation, multi-process TP run, or remote H20 validation was performed for this update.

## Sink loading-path follow-up

Updated commit: `6e171163ab008e15e7eca49f884633a66f26e3a8` (signed off; upstream `main` merged before committing).

The broader audit found a missed MiMo-V2 MTP path: it pre-sliced `attention_sink_bias` and then called the newly registered common loader, causing double TP sharding. At TP=2 with checkpoint `[0,...,7]`, the old path produced `[0,1,-inf,-inf]` and `[6,7,-inf,-inf]` instead of `[0,1,2,3]` and `[4,5,6,7]`. Removing this pre-slicing also fixes the inherited `MiMoV2OmniMTP` path.

Laguna and Qwen3-DFlash now register `load_attention_sink` on their sink parameters and pass the original checkpoint to normal loading. Their model-level sink preprocessing helpers were removed. The replicated visual sink in MiMo-V2 Omni and the multidimensional OpenPangu sink K/V parameters retain their existing loading contracts.

Test changes:

- Registration audit extended from five to seven attention implementations, adding Laguna and Qwen3-DFlash.
- One shared `test_attention_sink_model_loading_shards_once` covers MiMo-V2 MTP, Omni MTP, Laguna, and Qwen3-DFlash on both TP ranks. It calls the actual model loading entry points on minimal parameter containers, checks that the parameter loader receives the unsliced global checkpoint, and verifies cold-load values, layerwise reload values, and original sink storage.

Validation:

- Local isolated CPU execution: **31 passed** — 7 registration, 8 model loading-path, 3 GPT-OSS quant-path, 4 common reload, 4 shape, and 5 invalid-input cases.
- Restoring the old pre-slicing implementations in memory causes all **8** new loading-path cases to fail, confirming sensitivity to the reported regression.
- Ruff lint/format, diff whitespace, SPDX, forbidden-import, and CI test-tethering checks passed.
- Standard pytest was attempted again and remains blocked during `tests/conftest.py` import because the local Windows environment lacks `uvloop`. Complete pre-commit remains subject to the previously documented Windows hook limitation.

The temporary isolated harness executes the exact test functions with real PyTorch, the real reload modules and decorator, and production `AutoWeightsLoader`, `WeightsMapper`, model loading methods, and helpers extracted from source. Unrelated startup/platform dependencies and embedding/missing-layer types use stand-ins. The harness is not part of the PR, and these results do not constitute a standard-suite or full-model run. No remote H20, GPU execution, full-model evaluation, or multi-process TP run was performed.
